The dev's red test decides.)
Serial constraints cleared: `PR #34752 (roll-up summary read-only on update) is open on objectql's read-only rule: overlap-check against it before every push; no other in-flight claim of this seat on packages/objectql validation`
Pre-claim lane: `domain:server` — `packages/objectql/**`; routed to area o3-G by seat 3 (16:52Z)

Prior rulings read: delete,set_null,walk,clear,readonly,lookup,stripped,read-only,rule,rows,deleted,record → 273 hits; ADR-0148 D1 (recycle-bin restore under original ids: what a restore does with a set_null clear is read, not changed), ADR-0146 D11, ADR-0029 D9.7, ADR-0045 §6, ADR-0055 §1/§3, ADR-0056 D9 keyword-only; thread: triage 6953208762 only.

Lease `o3-G` (seat post #34584). Route: the strip lets through exactly the engine's referential clear: the field the walk is clearing, to null (or the multi-value lookup's remaining ids), on a write the engine marked with the operation-private `__referentialFieldClear` that a caller cannot forge through a transport. Every other read-only field in that write is still stripped, and no `isSystem` is granted to the walk.

## Claim amendment · 2026-11-17T18:19Z

Seat 3 widens the claim on this card to `packages/objectql/src/**/restore.ts` (ADR-0148 restore re-link), route A from o3-G's report on PR #34952. Why: once the set_null clear lands, restore's caller-context re-link of a readonly lookup is dropped by the static strip and logged DROPPED while `relinked` still counts it, leaving a silently unrestored link. Scope: a private re-link exemption of the same shape as the delete-side clear, `relinked` counting only landed re-links, plus two pins (re-link lands under caller context; a refused re-link is not counted). About 30 lines. Same PR, same L1-d delta; if the exemption changes what a caller can write, the PR declares it and the seat L2 follows.
